places.text: A salt road runs along the cliff, and the wind smells of the sea.
Rice terraces step down the hill like green mirrors. Frogs argue in every one of them.
You are at the edge of a market town, where the last stalls give way to cabbage fields.
A bamboo grove creaks around a narrow path. The light comes down in green stripes.
A ferry landing sits at the bend of a brown river: one rope, one post, and no ferry.
The yard of a roadside inn smells of horses, woodsmoke and yesterday's soup.
A pine ridge stands above the fog, and the needles are soft underfoot.
A small burned shrine stands by the road. Someone still leaves rice cakes on its step.
A millstream turns a wooden wheel that nobody seems to tend. The water is cold enough to hurt.
Old grave mounds rise on a hill behind a village, the grass on them cut neat by someone patient.
Reeds taller than you hiss in the wind across a wide marsh. The path is mostly a suggestion.
An old stone bridge arches over a dry gully. The moss on it is older than the kingdom.
Tea bushes cover the hills in neat rows. Pickers' baskets sit forgotten at the ends.
A mountain village clings to a slope. Chimney smoke rises straight up into still air.
A narrow valley is thick with wild herbs. Bees work it like tax collectors.
A mountain pass where bandits used to rule. Their wooden toll gate rots beside the road.
A waterfall drops into a deep green pool, and the spray hangs in the air like smoke.
The ruins of a sect outpost sit on a knoll, its wooden training posts still standing in rows.
Night falls over a wide river. Lantern boats drift far off, small as fireflies.
The grass thins into yellow sand at the edge of the western desert. The sky is enormous.
A temple hangs on a cliff face, held there by wooden beams and stubbornness.
A cave mouth breathes cold air into the summer heat. Old torch soot marks the stone.
A high pass still lies under snow. Your breath freezes on your collar.
Maples burn red along a mountain stream, and the leaves pile up in the eddies.
An abandoned border fort watches an empty plain. Crows hold court on the walls.
A field of rusted swords stands in the earth, each one marking a fighter nobody remembers.
A hot spring steams in a fold of the mountain. The rocks around it are warm to the touch.
Rain drums on the broad leaves of a southern forest. Everything is green and dripping.
A town stands empty, its doors open and its streets swept clean by the wind.
A pavilion stands on stilts in a quiet lake, reached by a zigzag walkway of planks.
You stand on a peak above the clouds. The world below is a white sea with islands.
A plateau lies scarred black by lightning. The air tastes of iron.
An ancient battlefield, where the grass grows in the shape of old trenches. Qi stirs here, uneasy.
A frozen lake lies in a crater, clear enough to see fish sleeping under the ice.
A crater where a star fell long ago. The stones still hum faintly.
A valley no map names. The trees are huge, and the silence is thick.
A forest so old the trunks stand like temple pillars. Sunlight never quite reaches the floor.
A mountain split in two by some old duel. The cut is as smooth as a table.
A spring rises where a spirit vein breaks the surface. The water glows a faint blue.
A natural stone bridge spans a chasm between two peaks. Wind howls underneath it.
You walk the rim of a sleeping volcano. Sulphur steam rises from cracks in the rock.
Cliffs of green jade rise over a gorge, polished smooth by a thousand years of wind.
A ring of old standing stones marks ground the sects call forbidden. Nothing grows inside it.
Silver dunes roll away under a full moon. The sand sings when the wind moves it.
The roofs of a sunken palace show above a still lake, their tiles green with weed.
You stand at a crossroads with a stone marker. Every arm of it has been worn blank.
A muddy road in steady rain. Your sandals have given up on dignity.
Golden fields wait for the harvest under a low autumn sun.
Willows lean over a slow river, and their long branches comb the water.
Stone stairs climb a mountain, thousands of them, worn into dips by pilgrims.
An old well stands alone in a field, far from any house.
A teahouse sits at the top of a long hill road, its banner faded to no colour at all.
A plum orchard is in blossom, and the petals drift across the path like slow snow.
A fishing village smells of salt and drying nets. The gulls watch you like creditors.
A forest at night. Owls trade gossip overhead, and the path glows pale in the moonlight.
Open grassland runs all the way to the sky. The wind never stops talking.
Outside the walls of a provincial city, carts wait in a long line at the gate.
A quiet temple courtyard with a single ginkgo tree, its leaves gold on the flagstones.
The floor of a red canyon, where the walls rise so high the sky is a ribbon.
Mist lies on a lake so thick that the far shore is only a rumour.
Jade stairs float in the open sky, each step a stride from the next, with nothing at all below.
A courtyard paved with cloud. Immortal officials pass with scrolls and do not look down.
The Peach Garden of the Heavens, where each tree takes three thousand years to fruit.
The Heavenly River runs above you, and its water is made of stars.
The halls of the celestial archive go on further than sight. The shelves hum softly.
A terrace where white cranes land and leave, carrying messages between the palaces.
Outside the Ministry of Thunder, drums the size of houses wait for their orders.
A lake of lotuses that open and close with every breath you take.
The Southern Heavenly Gate, where guards in gold armour stand as still as statues.
A hall of elixir furnaces, each one a bronze mountain breathing coloured smoke.
Islands float in a pale sky, joined by bridges of light.
A cold walk of white stone outside the Moon Palace. The light here has no source.
A hall where the threads of fate are spun. It sounds like rain falling on silk.
Stables where the dragons of the sky rest. The air is warm and smells of rain.
A platform at the edge of heaven where the sun is born each morning, small and red.
An immortal bazaar where pills, years and memories are traded under silk awnings.
A waterfall that falls upward into the clouds. The mist rises off it the wrong way.
The edge of the Upper Realm, where the clouds thin and the mortal world shows far below.
A grove of white jade bamboo. It chimes when the wind moves through it.
A palace where an old immortal has slept for ten thousand years. Everyone here whispers.
A meadow where the grass glows and springs back from every step.
A bell tower whose bell rings once a century. The ringer is waiting and visibly bored.
A corridor of red pillars bends nine times, and seems to end where it starts.
The heavenly kitchens, where dumplings are folded by servants older than mountains.
The Ministry of Rain, where clerks measure out the world's weather in jade cups.
A hollow under the roots that smells of earth and of you. Outside, the forest is waking.
Cold shallows over round stones. Small fish dart away from your shadow.
A hollow full of ferns, damp and dim. Every scent here is close and loud.
A narrow trail worn by smaller animals. It smells of fox, rabbit and old rain.
The edge of a human field. Their rows of plants are strange and very straight.
A sun-warmed rock shelf above the valley. You can see a long way, and nothing can creep up on you.
A mud bank by a slow river. Your tracks fill with water while you watch.
A thorn thicket, where nothing large can follow you.
A carpet of pine needles under tall trees. The resin smell is strong enough to taste.
Rain runs down the slope in little rivers. You shelter under a fallen trunk.
The outskirts of a human village: dogs, woodsmoke, and the smell of cooked rice.
A glade under the moon. The grass is silver, and the night insects sing.
The spine of the mountain: bare rock and wind. You can smell three valleys at once.
A deep river, green and strong. The current pulls at anything that touches it.
An old cave that remembers bears. The walls hold the cold of a hundred winters.
A ledge behind a waterfall. The roar fills your skull and hides your scent.
A slope burned last summer. New shoots push up through the black.
A high meadow full of flowers. Deer have grazed here this morning.
Rocks where humans tie ribbons and leave food for the mountain spirits. Possibly for you.
A stream half frozen, singing under its ice.
A cliff of old nests, where the wind comes up warm from the valley.
A sea of bamboo, swaying and creaking. The light moves in it like water.
A salt lick at the foot of a slope, trampled by every hoofed thing within a day's walk.
A peak in the clouds. The air is thin and thick with qi, and the sky is close enough to bite.
A deep pool in the mountains, dark and bottomless. The water hums with old power.
A ridge where storms are born. Lightning has fused the sand here into glass.
Sea cliffs under a grey sky. The waves boom into caves far below.
An ancient tree wider than a house. Its roots drink from a spirit vein.
A lake on a mountaintop that holds the whole sky in it.
A valley drowned in mist, where every sound comes from the wrong direction.
A vent where the mountain breathes warm. The rock glows red at the cracks.
A summit under too many stars. The qi of heaven falls here like dew.
A plain where humans fought long ago. The ground still tastes of iron.
The mouth of a great river, where fresh water meets the sea and the fish go mad.
A spring morning in the woods. Everything smells new, and most of it smells edible.
An autumn ridge, the leaves red and dry. Every step announces you.
A winter forest, white and silent. Your breath hangs in the air.
A summer marsh, loud with frogs and heavy with insects.
Reeds along a river. Herons stand in them like patient old monks.
A human road over the mountain. It smells of horses and iron and fear.
A ridge at night. The valley lights below are human fires, far and small.
A rocky gorge where the wind is trapped and goes round and round.
A wood of white birches, pale as bones in the dusk.
Rolling hills where cloud shadows run faster than any deer.
A valley after a storm. Water drips from everything, and the air smells sharp.

encounters.text: A small child sits by the road crying, holding one shoe. The other shoe is nowhere.

effects.log: You find it in a ditch. The child stops crying at once and runs off without a word. Children.

choices.text: Carry the child to the nearest house

effects.log: The family feeds you millet porridge. It is the best meal you have had all year.
You walk on. The crying follows you further than it should.

encounters.text: A peddler opens a box of pills and swears each one adds ten years to your life. The box looks less sure.

ok.log: It is a real qi pill, by accident. The peddler looks more surprised than you.

fail.log: It is chalk and honey. Your stomach files a complaint that lasts a day.

choices.text: Expose the fraud to the crowd

ok.log: The crowd takes back its money. One of them buys you a bun.

fail.log: The crowd sides with the peddler. Someone throws a turnip, accurately.

effects.log: Ten years for three coppers. If it were true, the peddler would be a god by now.

encounters.text: Three bandits step out with clubs and demand a road toll. Their leader has a cold and keeps sniffling.

effects.log: They count it twice, wish you a safe journey, and sneeze on the coins.

ok.log: They scatter into the trees. Their toll box is lighter than their reputation.

fail.log: Three clubs are more than one of you. You leave lighter and bruised.

choices.text: Offer the leader a cold remedy

ok.log: Ginger, honey, rest. The leader is touched and waves you through.

fail.log: They take the advice and the toll.

encounters.text: An elderly stranger sits over a stone go board and waves you into the empty seat.

ok.log: You win by one stone. The stranger laughs and shows you three moves you will remember forever.

fail.log: You lose badly, but slowly enough to learn something.

effects.log: The stranger nods and goes back to playing both sides, and losing to both.

choices.text: Watch a game from the side

effects.log: Two hours pass. You understand the board better and your legs not at all.

encounters.text: A thin yellow dog starts following you. It has decided you are its person.

effects.log: It eats, wags, and leaves the next morning with a better offer. Still, you feel lucky.
It goes, slowly, looking back the whole time. You feel like a villain.
It learns sit in an afternoon. You are prouder than you should be.

encounters.text: A wounded martial artist slumps against a tree, sword across the knees, watching you without blinking.

effects.log: At dawn they are gone, but a few stances are scratched in the dirt for you to study.
You sell it in the next town. It is not a proud day.
You never learn whether they lived. You think about it now and then.

encounters.text: Under a fallen log you spot a root shaped like a little person.

ok.log: It comes out whole, every hair root intact: wild ginseng.

fail.log: It snaps. You eat the pieces before they spoil. Not bad.

effects.log: Some things should be left to grow. The forest seems to agree.

encounters.text: A sudden downpour drives you under the eaves with a farmer, a monk and a goat.

effects.log: The monk explains breathing for an hour. The goat falls asleep. You do not.

choices.text: Help the farmer with the goat

effects.log: The goat has opinions. You win, eventually.
You wake dry, rested, and with the goat leaning on you.

encounters.text: A boy runs past you with a sack of rice. An angry shopkeeper runs after, much slower.

effects.log: The shopkeeper rewards you. The boy glares at you from the stocks.
The shopkeeper wheezes past. The boy is long gone, and maybe someone at home eats tonight.
The shopkeeper takes the money, confused. The boy, somewhere, will never know.

encounters.text: A young sect disciple, loud and bored, challenges anyone passing to a spar.

ok.log: You win. The disciple insists it was two out of three, then three out of five.

fail.log: You lose, but you learn where your stance is weak.

effects.log: The disciple calls you a coward. Three villagers laugh at them for it.

encounters.text: A blind fortune teller grabs your sleeve and says your future is very interesting.

effects.log: Great trials, great rewards, avoid eels. You feel oddly lucky all month.
The teller shouts that you will regret it. You probably will, a little.
A long pause, then laughter. Nobody has asked that in forty years.

encounters.text: A plank bridge groans under a cart of melons. The farmer pulling it looks at you hopefully.

effects.log: The cart crosses. Your back complains for a week.

ok.log: The bridge holds because you do. The farmer tells everyone.

fail.log: The bridge gives. You, the farmer and the melons all end up in the stream.

effects.log: The cart makes it. The melon is excellent.

encounters.text: A light bobs among the trees at dusk, too slow for a firefly and too low for a star.

ok.log: It leads you to a spring where the water tastes of moonlight.

fail.log: It leads you in circles until dawn, then goes out.

effects.log: Old wisdom: lights in the woods are someone else's problem.

encounters.text: A drunk poet staggers along, reciting verses to anyone who stands still long enough.

effects.log: Most are bad. One is so good it stays with you for years.

choices.text: Answer with a verse of your own

ok.log: The poet weeps and declares you a genius to the whole road.

fail.log: The poet corrects your rhyme scheme at length.

effects.log: The poet sleeps on the way. You are thanked by a tired family.

encounters.text: A wandering monk asks you for a bowl of rice and offers a lesson in breathing in return.

effects.log: The lesson takes three breaths. You use it for the rest of your life.
The monk bows anyway and moves on. You feel smaller than the rice was.

encounters.text: A fat green snake lies across the path, sunning itself in no hurry at all.

effects.log: It takes an hour. You learn patience, or at least practise it.

ok.log: It does not even look up.

fail.log: It looks up. Then it bites.

ok.log: The apothecary pays well for snake gall.

fail.log: The snake catches you instead, in a sense.

encounters.text: A sealed letter lies in the dust, addressed to someone in the next town.

effects.log: The addressee cries with joy and pays you a few coppers. You never learn why.
It is a dumpling recipe, guarded like a state secret. It is a good recipe.
Someone else's story. You let the wind have it.

encounters.text: Two masked figures drop from the trees, blades out. They glance at each other: wrong target, perhaps.

ok.log: They run. Whoever they were hunting owes you a drink.

fail.log: They were the right target after all, in their opinion.

ok.log: They apologise, bow, and vanish. Professionals.

fail.log: They take your purse for the trouble.

ok.log: You are gone before they decide.

fail.log: A thrown knife finds your shoulder on the way.

encounters.text: A recruiter from a minor sect hands you a pamphlet promising glory, three meals a day and a roof.

choices.text: Hear the pitch over free lunch

effects.log: The lunch is real. The glory is less certain.
It is porridge. It was always going to be porridge.
The recruiter thanks you and rewrites the pamphlets. Your name is in the new one.

encounters.text: Two fighters duel in a clearing while a crowd shouts advice neither of them wants.

effects.log: Each mistake they make is one you will not.

ok.log: Both swords stop on yours. The crowd goes quiet, then cheers.

fail.log: Both swords stop on you.

effects.log: It is a good afternoon for tea.

encounters.text: A merchant swears the bronze mirror on the cart shows your past life. For a price.

effects.log: You see a tired ox in a field. It explains a great deal.

ok.log: You get a look for half price. Still an ox.

fail.log: The price goes up as you talk.

effects.log: Whatever you were, you are this now. That is enough to manage.

encounters.text: A stranger sits cross-legged with dark veins standing out on the neck. Their qi is running wild.

choices.text: Steady them with your own qi

ok.log: The veins fade. The stranger bows to the ground and tells everyone.

fail.log: Their wild qi floods back into you. You both survive, barely.

effects.log: By dawn it has passed. They thank you weakly for staying.
Qi deviation can spread to the careless. You tell yourself that.

encounters.text: A fox with too many tails watches you from a rock, trots off, stops, and looks back.

ok.log: It leads you to a hollow where the qi is sweet as rice wine.

fail.log: It leads you into brambles and laughs, in its fashion.

effects.log: The fox bows back. You are fairly sure it bowed back.
Wise. Probably.

encounters.text: A caravan master needs one more guard for the road to the next town, and is not fussy.

effects.log: Two bandit scares and one real fight later, you are paid.

ok.log: Double pay, and you get the good camel.

fail.log: The master hires someone cheaper, then hires you at half rate.

effects.log: The caravan rolls off. You keep your own pace.

encounters.text: A torn page from a martial manual flaps against a bush. The diagrams are half rubbed out.

ok.log: The missing half fills itself in, in your head.

fail.log: You guess the missing half wrong. Your meridians object.

effects.log: You fold it carefully into your sleeve.
Some knowledge is cursed. Some is just badly drawn. Either way, it is ash.

encounters.text: A brawl spills out of a tavern door: benches, cups and one very surprised chicken.

ok.log: You are the last one standing, which is a kind of fame.

fail.log: A bench finds you first.

effects.log: The chicken is grateful in the way chickens are, which is not at all. You feel good anyway.
The owner pays you in coins and leftover dumplings.

encounters.text: A pocket of thick, cold qi gathers around you, the kind that freezes careless meridians.

ok.log: You guide the cold through every channel. It leaves you sharp and clear.

fail.log: The cold bites deep. You gain a little and shiver for a week.

effects.log: Just one. Enough.
You know your limits. That too is cultivation.

encounters.text: Two drunk fighters insist you swear eternal kinship with them on the spot.

effects.log: They are delighted and forget it all by morning. You do not.
They are wounded. Deeply. For about a minute.

ok.log: They wake under the table. You wake as a legend.

fail.log: You wake under the table. They do not remember either.

encounters.text: A hunter's iron trap has caught a white deer. The deer looks at you and does not struggle.

effects.log: It limps off. That night you dream of a white forest and wake strangely lucky.
The hunter has a family. So, perhaps, does the deer.

choices.text: Wait for the hunter and talk

effects.log: The hunter lets it go, grumbling, for a few of your coins.

encounters.text: A teahouse keeper serves you tea that smells faintly of almonds. The keeper smiles too much.

ok.log: Your body burns the poison off in a sweat. You leave a large tip, which frightens everyone.

fail.log: You spend three days learning what almonds can do.

choices.text: Swap the cups when the keeper looks away

ok.log: The keeper drinks and confesses everything to the guards.

fail.log: The keeper notices. There is a scuffle.

effects.log: You leave no tip. That will teach them.

encounters.text: A young noble's carriage has lost a wheel. The noble seems never to have seen mud before.

effects.log: The noble pays you generously, holding the coins by the edges.

choices.text: Teach the noble to fix it

effects.log: Mud, sweat, a fixed wheel and a new expression. Worth it.
You hear the shouting for a long way down the road.

encounters.text: A bounty notice flutters on a post. The sketched face looks familiar, and slightly like yours.

effects.log: Nobody saw. Probably.

ok.log: You find the outlaw in two days. The bounty is yours.

fail.log: The outlaw finds you first.

effects.log: It does not suit you. It does keep you out of trouble.

encounters.text: A red bird lands on your shoulder and refuses to leave for most of a morning.

effects.log: It eats from your hand and leaves at noon. The day goes well after that.
It answers none. People stare at you all morning.
Children follow you. So does a rumour that you are blessed.

encounters.text: A disciple from a rival school blocks your way, eager to find out whether you are worth hating.

ok.log: You are worth hating. They are pleased.

fail.log: You are not, they decide, and leave you sore.

ok.log: By the second cup you are friends. By the third, rivals again, but friendly ones.

fail.log: They pour it on your shoes.

effects.log: They shout after you for a while. You have a nice walk.

encounters.text: An old master in a straw cloak asks you one question about the nature of the sword, and waits.

ok.log: The master nods once. Something in you settles a long way down.

fail.log: The master sighs. Your answer was honest, at least.

ok.log: The master blocks with a chopstick, laughs, and gives you a lesson.

fail.log: The master blocks with a chopstick, and the lesson is your face.

effects.log: The master smiles. Sometimes that is the answer.

encounters.text: Clouds gather overhead, dark and personal. Someone's tribulation is coming, maybe yours.

ok.log: Lightning runs through you and out, leaving you tempered.

fail.log: Lightning runs through you and stays a while.

effects.log: It was not yours. Someone in the next valley has a very bad afternoon.

encounters.text: Banners of two sects lie trampled together. The fight is over; the wounded are not.

choices.text: Tend the wounded of both sides

effects.log: Both sides will remember who came to help.
You find one under a body. It is not a proud find.
Their war. You hope it stays theirs.

encounters.text: A cultivator with red eyes and a pleasant voice offers to teach you a faster way.

effects.log: The method works. It also smells of blood.

ok.log: The demonic cultivator flees, and a village sleeps easier.

fail.log: The pleasant voice stops being pleasant.

effects.log: They laugh softly. The road feels colder for a mile.

encounters.text: Your own shadow peels off the ground and takes a stance. It knows all your moves.

ok.log: You win by doing something you have never done before.

fail.log: It wins by doing everything you always do.

effects.log: It bows back and lies down again, satisfied.
It points at your weak side and fades. Fair.

encounters.text: Lines of an ancient formation surface in the earth, glowing as you step near.

ok.log: The pattern unfolds in your mind like a map.

fail.log: The formation notices you studying it.

ok.log: It shatters, and its stored qi rushes into you.

fail.log: It does not break. You do, slightly.

effects.log: It glows a little sadly as you go.

encounters.text: A young fighter has followed you for three days and finally asks to become your student.

effects.log: One lesson, taught well. The youngster leaves glowing.
They go, crying. Their parents will thank you.
They pass. You still send them home, with a letter to a good school.

encounters.text: Two experts are about to kill each other over a glowing fruit on the branch between them.

ok.log: You eat it in one bite before either moves. Your qi roars.

fail.log: They stop fighting each other at once, which is worse.

ok.log: You split the fruit. Both remember your fairness.

fail.log: Both decide you are the problem.

effects.log: Very instructive. Neither of them gets the fruit; a bird does.

encounters.text: A tiger made of white lightning stalks out of the rain. It is curious, which is worse than hungry.

ok.log: It circles, sniffs, and leaves you a spark of its strength.

fail.log: It decides to play.

effects.log: It drinks and pads off into the storm.

encounters.text: A tomb door stands ajar. The seal on it was broken recently, and from the inside.

ok.log: Whatever left did not take everything. You find a spirit stone.

fail.log: Whatever left came back.

effects.log: It takes most of your qi and all of your nerve.
Very fast.

encounters.text: A sword stuck in the rock hums as you pass. It seems to be choosing.

ok.log: It comes free with a sound like a waking bird, then crumbles, its last strength yours.

fail.log: It does not choose you, and says so through your hands.

effects.log: It hums at a different pitch. You understand a little of what swords want.
Someone else, someday. You wish them luck.

encounters.text: A grim young fighter blocks the road and declares an ancestral grudge against you. The details are vague.

ok.log: The grudge ends where it began: vague and on the ground.

fail.log: The grudge is satisfied. You are not.

ok.log: They are thrown completely and leave confused.

fail.log: That makes it worse somehow.

effects.log: After an awkward talk, they admit they have the wrong person.

encounters.text: The wind changes, and for one breath you hear how all things move together.

effects.log: You sit until the stars come out. Your qi moves like the wind now.
The words are clumsy. The understanding is not.
It fades, but you walk differently.

encounters.text: A merchant sells lifespan in small jars. The labels are honest, which is unsettling.

effects.log: It tastes of someone's spring. You feel younger and somewhat guilty.

choices.text: Ask where the years come from

effects.log: The merchant smiles and says nothing. That is an answer.

choices.text: Report the merchant to the sects

effects.log: The merchant is gone by morning. The jars too.

encounters.text: The qi of heaven and earth goes wild for an hour, roaring like a river in spring.

ok.log: You drink the flood and do not burst.

fail.log: You drink too much, too fast.

choices.text: Guide some of it into the land

effects.log: Fields nearby will bear well for years.

encounters.text: An imperial envoy with a scroll is looking for experts of your level. The pay is very good.

effects.log: A border bandit chief, a long ride, a short fight. You are paid well.
The envoy bows. The emperor will not remember you, which has its uses.

choices.text: Pretend to be weaker than you are

ok.log: The envoy believes you. Peace and quiet.

fail.log: The envoy sees through it and tells everyone.

encounters.text: A wooden puppet with a cracked mask walks the road alone, its master's strings trailing behind it.

ok.log: It breaks into ordinary wood. A cold qi escapes into the sky.

fail.log: It fights back with someone else's skill.

effects.log: They lead to an empty chair. You learn much from the chair.
It walks out of sight, still searching for its master.

encounters.text: The stars line up strangely tonight. Even you can almost read the warning in them.

effects.log: You learn something true and lose a night's sleep.
Whatever it was, it happens to someone else.

encounters.text: A noodle stall appears out of nowhere. The cook nods as if you were expected.

effects.log: The best noodles of your life. When you look back, the stall is gone.

ok.log: The cook whispers one secret. It involves patience.

fail.log: The cook laughs, and you laugh too, and that is all you get.

encounters.text: A black cat crosses your path, stops, and crosses it again the other way, very deliberately.

ok.log: It leads you to a jade charm lying in the grass.

fail.log: It leads you into a nettle patch, deliberately.

effects.log: The cat accepts this as its due.
The cat stares. You have entered a negotiation you do not understand.

encounters.text: A storm hits fast, and you spend the day under a ledge, counting the thunder.

effects.log: The thunder sets a rhythm. Your breath follows.
Wet, cold, and better at it.
Thunder is the best lullaby. You wake rested.

encounters.text: A gang of village children decide you are the monster in their game.

effects.log: You lose, heroically, many times. The children are delighted.
Twenty small fighters practise it badly and proudly.
They chase you for a mile. It is surprisingly good training.

encounters.text: A merchant has lost the road and most of their dignity, and asks you the way.

effects.log: They pay you, and throw in a pair of sandals.
They thank you and walk confidently in the wrong direction.
You learn which roads are dangerous and which inns are honest.

encounters.text: An ox has escaped its farm and stands in the road, enormous and very pleased with itself.

ok.log: The farmer is an old soldier with a limp. For the ox, eggs; for the way you handled it, a bundle in oilcloth from the rafters: the spear manual of the frontier, from the years before the farm. "It is no use to an ox," the farmer says.

fail.log: The ox leads you instead, into a pond.

ok.log: A glorious ride. People talk about it for weeks.

fail.log: A short ride.

effects.log: The ox will go home when the ox wants.

encounters.text: A seed falls into your palm from nowhere. It is warm, and seems to have a heartbeat.

ok.log: It blooms in your dantian like a lamp.

fail.log: It disagrees with you for a week.

effects.log: Years later, you hear of a tree there whose fruit heals fevers.

encounters.text: A funeral procession passes in white, with drums and paper money in the air.

effects.log: The chief mourner bows back. A small grace on a grey day.

choices.text: Join the mourners for a while

effects.log: Nobody asks who you are. Grief is generous with company.
You have had enough funerals of your own.

encounters.text: Someone bumps into you and apologises a little too warmly.

ok.log: Your purse comes back, with someone else's as interest.

fail.log: They twist free, with your purse.

effects.log: Your purse is lighter. So, oddly, is your heart.

encounters.text: A stone carved with a single character stands by the roadside. The stroke has the weight of a sword cut.

effects.log: One stroke, one breath, one cut. You understand a little more.

ok.log: Your copy is not bad. Your hand moves differently after.

fail.log: Your copy is bad. Your qi wobbles trying.

encounters.text: A wedding procession blocks the road with music, rice wine and a lot of shouting.

effects.log: You eat, toast, and are briefly someone's cousin.
The families are touched. Good luck follows a gift, they say.
It takes all afternoon. The music is good, at least.

encounters.text: Wolves howl close, then closer. Something on the wind has made them brave.

effects.log: A cold night in a tree. The wolves leave at dawn, bored.

ok.log: They test the fire, then you, then leave.

fail.log: One gets through before they break.

ok.log: They go quiet. A very confused pack.

fail.log: They take it as an invitation.

encounters.text: A hermit sitting on a stone says they will answer one question, but only one.

effects.log: The answer is short and annoying, and true.
The hermit taps your forehead. Things go well for a while.
Nobody has asked in years. They talk until dark, and give you tea.

encounters.text: A cart of pottery has overturned, and the potter sits among the pieces, very quiet.

effects.log: Half survive. In the false bottom of the biggest broken jar is a wax-sealed book: the potter's grandfather hid it there and never said why. "It was meant for whoever helped," the potter says, and will not take it back.
You carry a teapot for a month, out of kindness.

choices.text: Mend a bowl with a little qi

effects.log: A clumsy repair. The potter keeps it on a shelf, they say, for luck.

encounters.text: A message pigeon lands at your feet, exhausted, a tiny tube tied to its leg.

effects.log: Prices of salt in a far city. Not worth the guilt.

choices.text: Rest it and send it on

effects.log: It flies off at dawn, strong again.

choices.text: Add a note of your own

effects.log: Somewhere, someone gets salt prices and a kind word from a stranger.

encounters.text: An old couple bicker beside the road over the right way to fold a dumpling.

ok.log: Both agree you are wise and feed you to prove it.

fail.log: Both agree you are wrong.

effects.log: Diplomacy. They make both kinds.

encounters.text: A pale figure in very old clothes stands by the roadside and asks what year it is.

effects.log: They thank you, sigh, and fade into the morning.
You do not look back. You do not need to.
They tell you a year long gone. You both laugh, uneasily.

encounters.text: A wild persimmon tree hangs heavy with fruit, and nobody seems to own it.

effects.log: Sweet, cold, perfect.

choices.text: Climb for the best one at the top

ok.log: The best one is the best one.

fail.log: The branch has its own opinion.

effects.log: Fruit is fruit, and coins are coins.

encounters.text: A junior immortal has lost the scroll they were sent to deliver, and is pretending to inspect a cloud.

effects.log: You find it under a sleeping crane. The junior owes you forever.
Efficient. The junior will not forget, in either sense.

ok.log: Your copy is better than the original.

fail.log: Forgery in heaven is noticed.

encounters.text: A monkey in official robes is stuffing heavenly peaches into its sleeves.

ok.log: The monkey is caught. The garden keepers bow to you for a century.

fail.log: The monkey is faster, and throws peach stones.

ok.log: It shares, grinning. The peach is a thousand springs in one bite.

fail.log: It throws one at your head.

effects.log: Some officials are best left to their sleeves.

encounters.text: A herald calls your name. A minor star lord wishes to see you, at once or sooner.

effects.log: The audience is short and kind. You leave known.

ok.log: The star lord admires your calm.

fail.log: The star lord does not.

choices.text: Bring a gift of your own qi

effects.log: A small lamp of your qi, offered with both hands. It is remembered.

encounters.text: Heavenly dew forms on the leaves at dawn, each drop heavy with qi.

effects.log: Cold, bright, and full of morning.
The sick immortals thank you. Yes, immortals get sick.

encounters.text: Two immortal scholars debate whether the void has a back side. They want you to judge.

ok.log: Your ruling is quoted for a thousand years.

fail.log: Your ruling is quoted for a thousand years, mockingly.

effects.log: They unite against you, which ends the debate.
They are still debating when you pass again a decade later.

encounters.text: A cloud horse has thrown its rider and gallops loose, kicking up thunder.

ok.log: You bring it down to a walk. The rider owes you.

fail.log: It drags you through three clouds.

ok.log: It nuzzles you and steams gently.

fail.log: It kicks thunder at you.

encounters.text: A prayer drifts up from the mortal world, faint and earnest, and lands at your feet.

effects.log: Far below, a sick child gets better. You feel lighter.

choices.text: Pass it to the right office

effects.log: It will be answered in time. Heavenly time.
A rice harvest, a cough, a lost goat. You remember being mortal.

encounters.text: An immortal who ascended one day before you reminds you of it, loudly and often.

ok.log: A day is not much, it turns out.

fail.log: A day is enough, it turns out.

effects.log: Eternity is long. You can wait them out.

ok.log: They leave flustered. The court laughs.

fail.log: They have had more practice.

encounters.text: A sleeping sky dragon breathes out a cloud that smells of rain and old dreams.

effects.log: You dream for a moment of seas older than the world.
A dragon's dream is a dragon's business.

encounters.text: A loose thread of fate hangs in the air, glowing. Somebody's life is unravelling.

ok.log: Somewhere below, a stranger does not fall.

fail.log: The knot slips, and burns your fingers.

effects.log: The weavers bow and mend it. They will remember your name.

ok.log: It was yours. You feel your road shift kindly.

fail.log: It was yours. You feel your road shift.

encounters.text: An alchemist of heaven asks you to taste a new pill. They promise it is probably safe.

ok.log: It is wonderful. They name it after you.

fail.log: It is not safe. They name it after you anyway.

effects.log: They taste it themselves, and turn briefly blue.
A long list, half of it beautiful, half of it terrifying.

encounters.text: A jade rabbit sits in your path, pounding something in a tiny mortar, very seriously.

effects.log: Hours later, a pill of moonlight. It gives you a crumb.
It explains for an hour. You understand some of it.
It does not look up. Serious work.

encounters.text: A clerk informs you that your ascension paperwork is missing three seals.

ok.log: Three offices, three seals, one century. Done.

fail.log: Four offices, two seals, and a new form.

ok.log: The clerk finds the seals in a drawer.

fail.log: The clerk adds a fourth seal.

effects.log: The queue is long enough for real progress.

encounters.text: A small star falls from its place and rolls to a stop at your feet, embarrassed.

choices.text: Put it back in the sky

ok.log: It hangs where it belongs, twinkling at you.

fail.log: It is heavier than it looks.

choices.text: Keep it warm until someone comes

effects.log: It glows against you for an afternoon.

encounters.text: An old god with no temples left sits alone, polishing a crown nobody worships.

effects.log: Stories of a forgotten age. You leave wiser and sadder.

choices.text: Offer a prayer of your own

effects.log: The god smiles. It has been a long time.
The god nods. Courtesy is never forgotten here.

encounters.text: An invitation to a banquet of the immortals floats down to you, written in light.

effects.log: Wine of a thousand years, music like water.
A gift of your own qi. The host remembers it.
Some banquets last a decade. You have things to do.

encounters.text: Heavenly soldiers drill in ranks of ten thousand, and an officer invites you to join a round.

effects.log: Ten thousand spears, one breath. You learn what one breath means.
The patterns are beautiful from above.

encounters.text: An immortal fishes off the edge of a cloud, the line dropping toward the mortal world.

ok.log: You catch a lost wish. It tastes of childhood.

fail.log: You catch a mortal's hat.

effects.log: Prayers, mostly. Sometimes a kite.

encounters.text: A mirror of karma hangs in a corridor. Everyone walks past it quickly.

ok.log: You see your whole road, and forgive most of it.

fail.log: You see your whole road. It is a lot.

effects.log: There is wisdom in crowds.

encounters.text: A qilin foal has wandered off and stands nuzzling your sleeve.

effects.log: Its mother bows a horned head to you.
Flowers bloom wherever it steps. Your day is very good.

encounters.text: A great bell rings once somewhere, and every immortal nearby stops to count.

effects.log: Silence, then a breath. You have joined a ritual older than mountains.
Nobody remembers. They count anyway.

encounters.text: Two court immortals whisper that a high seat will soon be empty.

effects.log: You learn who is rising and who is falling.
You are popular for a day.

choices.text: Warn the holder of the seat

effects.log: They survive the scheme and remember you.

encounters.text: An apprentice of the Thunder Ministry drops a bolt, which starts hopping about on its own.

ok.log: It crackles in your fist and goes still.

fail.log: It catches you instead.

effects.log: It is found in a teapot. Everyone is relieved.

encounters.text: An immortal you have never met greets you like an old friend, then realises the mistake too late.

effects.log: You spend a pleasant afternoon as someone else.
They laugh, embarrassed, and buy you tea anyway.

encounters.text: A furnace boy spills a cauldron, and a fragrant cloud of half-made elixir rolls your way.

ok.log: Half an elixir is still an elixir.

fail.log: Half an elixir is also half a poison.

effects.log: The furnace boy keeps the job, thanks to you.

encounters.text: A garden immortal is losing a war with weeds that grow a foot every time they are cut.

choices.text: Pull them up by the root

ok.log: Roots and all. The garden immortal weeps with joy.

fail.log: The weeds pull back.

effects.log: They agree to grow elsewhere. Heaven is strange.

encounters.text: An examiner of the heavens offers you a surprise test on the classics of the Dao.

ok.log: Top marks. Your name goes up on a jade board.

fail.log: Your name goes up on a different board.

effects.log: The examiner pencils you in for a hundred years from now.

encounters.text: A shower of shooting stars streams past, close enough to warm your face.

ok.log: It burns in your hand and becomes part of your qi.

fail.log: It burns in your hand.

effects.log: Here, wishes are a form of paperwork. Yours is filed.

encounters.text: Music drifts from a hidden pavilion, each note shaping the clouds as it passes.

effects.log: It leads you nowhere, beautifully.

ok.log: The hidden musician answers your tune.

fail.log: The music stops, pointedly.

encounters.text: Far off, at the very top of the heavens, someone very important looks your way for a moment.

effects.log: The glance moves on. You are, perhaps, noted.

ok.log: The glance lingers. Someone smiles.

fail.log: The glance hardens. You feel it for a year.

effects.log: Some attention is better avoided.

encounters.text: A hawk's shadow slides over the ground, and your whole body freezes.

effects.log: The shadow passes. You remember how to breathe.

ok.log: You make it. Your heart is louder than the wind.

fail.log: Talons rake you before you reach the brush.

ok.log: The hawk swerves, startled. Small and fierce, then.

fail.log: The hawk is not impressed.

encounters.text: A bush hangs heavy with red berries. The birds have not touched them, which is suspicious.

ok.log: Sweet and full of sun. The birds were wrong.

fail.log: The birds were right.

effects.log: It spits them out. You learn a smell to avoid.

encounters.text: A human child spots you and holds out a rice ball, very slowly.

effects.log: The rice is sticky and kind. The child laughs.
The child is left holding a rice ball and a good story.
The child drops the rice and flees. You eat it anyway.

encounters.text: A wildcat twice your size sniffs the air. It has not seen you yet.

ok.log: You leave nothing for it to smell.

fail.log: The wind turns.

ok.log: It decides you are not worth it.

fail.log: It decides you are.

encounters.text: The full moon rises, and a thread of cold qi comes down with it.

effects.log: Cold and bright. Something in you grows.
By dawn, you understand the moon a little.

encounters.text: A human snare lies hidden in the grass. You smell the iron and the hands that set it.

choices.text: Set it off from a distance

effects.log: Snap. One less trap in the forest.
The small animals avoid it now.
You remember the smell of iron and hands.

encounters.text: Something small and fast rustles in the grass. Your stomach has opinions.

ok.log: Dinner.

fail.log: Nothing. It was a leaf all along.

effects.log: Slow is faster. You eat well.

encounters.text: Another young beast claims this patch, puffing itself up and squeaking threats.

ok.log: It flees. The patch is yours.

fail.log: You flee. The patch is its.

effects.log: Two is warmer than one.
Plenty of patches in the world.

encounters.text: Rain comes hard, and the ground starts to run away under you.

effects.log: Wet and miserable, but high.

ok.log: You come out downstream, soaked and alive.

fail.log: The water is stronger than you.

encounters.text: Your bones ache and your skin itches. Something in you wants to be bigger.

effects.log: You wake larger. Just a little.
It never stops, but you run faster.

encounters.text: An old tortoise watches you with deep, unhurried eyes, as if waiting for a question.

effects.log: You sit until sunset. Something passes between you.
It withdraws, deeply disappointed in you.

encounters.text: A gang of crows has decided you are a problem, and is telling the whole valley.

effects.log: They get bored eventually. Crows always do.

ok.log: They scatter, insulted.

fail.log: They peck you in turns.

ok.log: A bright button. You do not know why you want it, but you do.

fail.log: They want it more.

encounters.text: A woodcutter rests on a stump and hums. The axe lies within reach, but the hands are tired.

effects.log: You learn the song.

ok.log: The woodcutter stares, then laughs, then shares lunch.

fail.log: The axe comes up.

encounters.text: Human hunters with bows and dogs are working the slope, and the dogs have your scent.

ok.log: They chase your scent into a bog. The dogs are furious.

fail.log: The dogs are cleverer than you thought.

ok.log: One great sound, and they run. They will tell stories.

fail.log: The arrows fly first.

effects.log: They pass within a stone's throw.

encounters.text: A spirit herb glows in a crack in the rock, and its scent goes straight to your core.

effects.log: Warmth spreads through your whole body.
Next year it will be stronger. You will remember.

encounters.text: A rival beast, scarred and confident, wants this territory and has come to say so.

ok.log: It leaves with a new scar.

fail.log: You leave with your first.

ok.log: It looks away first.

fail.log: It does not.

effects.log: There is other ground. You eat well that night anyway.

encounters.text: A village shaman leaves rice wine and a boiled pig's head on a rock, bowing toward you.

effects.log: Wine and pork. Being a spirit has its benefits.
Their harvest will be good this year.
The shaman bows anyway, and leaves it for the crows.

encounters.text: A human traveller is lost in the cold and sitting down. Sitting down is how they die.

effects.log: They follow your shape through the snow to a village.
They wake, alive, and remember you forever.
The cold is the cold. You walk on.

encounters.text: Smoke on the wind. Somewhere upslope, the forest has caught.

effects.log: You run with every other living thing.
Rabbits, mice, a lost fawn. You come out singed.

ok.log: Clouds gather and break over the fire.

fail.log: The sky does not listen.

encounters.text: A monk meditates on a rock and does not stir, even when you come close enough to breathe on.

effects.log: Two stillnesses together. You learn something about breathing.
The monk does not stir. Perhaps the monk is still smiling.
Some things should not be interrupted.

encounters.text: An old voice speaks in your head from somewhere under the earth: "Not yet, little one."

effects.log: Nothing else. But you feel watched over.

ok.log: A deep laugh, and warmth rises through the ground.

fail.log: The earth shrugs.

encounters.text: Lightning splits a tree beside you. Everything on you stands on end.

ok.log: It burns all the way down and becomes yours.

fail.log: It burns all the way down.

effects.log: Sensible.

encounters.text: A pit trap opens under you. You hang over the stakes by sheer stubbornness.

ok.log: You come out and smash the pit in.

fail.log: You come out, but not cleanly.

ok.log: A root gives you a hold.

fail.log: The edge crumbles first.

encounters.text: Rain falls from a clear sky. The old stories say the foxes are marrying somewhere.

effects.log: Warm rain is a kind of luck.

ok.log: You glimpse lanterns in the woods and hear laughter.

fail.log: You find only wet ferns.

encounters.text: A herder's calf has wandered from the herd and is bawling for its mother.

effects.log: The herder sees you and does not shout.
The herder will tell this story with a different ending.
It finds its own way, eventually.

encounters.text: The god of this mountain comes to look at you: a tall shape of mist and pine scent.

effects.log: The mountain approves.

ok.log: The god nods. Equals, then.

fail.log: The god disagrees, firmly.

effects.log: The god accepts and teaches you a secret of stone.

encounters.text: A human army marches through the valley below: ten thousand torches and one stubborn general.

effects.log: Human wars are human business.

ok.log: Ten thousand torches stop. The stories begin.

fail.log: Arrows. A great many arrows.

ok.log: They march in circles and go home.

fail.log: The fog drains you and they march on.

encounters.text: A tribulation cloud gathers, small and black and aimed at you alone.

ok.log: Lightning, again and again. You are still here.

fail.log: Lightning, again and again.

effects.log: It passes. It will return, when you are ready.

encounters.text: A human sorcerer draws binding talismans in the air at you, with shaking hands.

ok.log: Paper and ink burn. The sorcerer runs.

fail.log: The talismans hold a while.

ok.log: The sorcerer lowers the brush, and you talk until dawn.

fail.log: The sorcerer panics.

effects.log: You are gone. The talisman binds a pine tree.

encounters.text: Below, a village's fields are cracked with drought. The people look up at the sky, and at you.

effects.log: Clouds come at your call. The people weep in the downpour.
The sky is not yours to command. Or not yet.
A spring where you scratch the earth. A well by evening.

encounters.text: A messenger of a human king kneels at a distance and asks you to protect the realm.

effects.log: A promise to a king. Kings remember promises.
The messenger leaves, pale. You owe no one.
Cattle arrive every spring after that.

encounters.text: An ancient beast of another kind passes through your territory, enormous and polite.

ok.log: It tells you of lands beyond the sea.

fail.log: It does not notice you.

ok.log: It bows, amused, and yields the path.

fail.log: It is not amused.

effects.log: Some guests should be let through.

encounters.text: Humans have built a small shrine to you. The carving looks nothing like you.

effects.log: Incense and prayers. They mean well.
Overnight, the carving changes. The village is amazed.
They rebuild it, bigger and more frightened.

encounters.text: A storm is driving a fishing fleet onto the rocks, and you can feel every small hull.

effects.log: The water goes flat. The fishers will never forget.

ok.log: Boat by boat. They tell your story for centuries.

fail.log: The storm is stronger than you tonight.

effects.log: Some boats make it. Some do not. The sea is the sea.

encounters.text: Deep under the mountains, a great qi vein is shifting. You feel it like a second heartbeat.

ok.log: You drink from the vein at its source.

fail.log: The earth closes behind you for a while.

ok.log: The land above stays green.

fail.log: It moves anyway, and you with it.

effects.log: It settles in your dreams.

encounters.text: A grey-haired hunter, the last of a long family of hunters, comes alone with an old bow.

ok.log: The bow breaks. The family line of hunters ends here.

fail.log: The old bow is still good.

choices.text: Let the hunter see you, then leave

effects.log: The hunter lowers the bow and goes home to tell it.
The hunter waits until dusk, then leaves.

encounters.text: A thread of light from the heavens touches your brow, and for a moment you hear the Upper Realm.

ok.log: A glimpse of something beyond. You are changed.

fail.log: The light is too bright.

effects.log: There will be time.

encounters.text: A rainbow stands over the valley, so solid you could almost climb it.

effects.log: It fades slowly. You feel lucky.
You never reach it, but you run very fast.

encounters.text: Fish leap upstream in a silver rush, and the water is alive with them.

effects.log: You eat until you can barely move.
One leaps higher than the rest. You understand something about wanting.

encounters.text: A wild bees' nest hangs from a branch, dripping honey and menace.

ok.log: Honey. Worth every sting.

fail.log: Stings. Not worth the honey.

effects.log: The bees hum approval.

encounters.text: A human voice sings in the distance, some old song about a mountain and someone lost.

effects.log: The song stays with you for days.

choices.text: Sing back in your own way

ok.log: The singer stops, then answers.

fail.log: The singer runs.

encounters.text: A lost young thing of some other kind follows you, squeaking.

effects.log: It grows fat on your leftovers.
Its family finds it. They bow, in their way.
It squeaks off. You feel a little cold.

encounters.text: A scent you have never smelled drifts by, sweet and metallic and impossible to ignore.

ok.log: A fallen star, still warm. You breathe its qi.

fail.log: A human trap, baited.

effects.log: You will know it next time.

encounters.text: The night is clear and full of stars, and the qi of heaven falls like fine snow.

effects.log: You glow faintly until dawn.
Stars move in ways you can almost read.

encounters.text: A campfire flickers. Humans laugh around it, and the smell of roasting meat drifts out.

ok.log: Gone before they see. Their stories grow.

fail.log: Someone throws a burning branch.

effects.log: You learn how humans laugh.

choices.text: Make a noise in the dark

effects.log: They do not sleep tonight.

encounters.text: The ground shakes. Rocks fall. Birds burst out of every tree at once.

effects.log: You make it.
The earth tells you something about itself.

ok.log: Nothing moves you.

fail.log: A rock finds you.

encounters.text: An old deer lies down in the grass to die, calm, as if it chose the spot.

effects.log: You stay till the end. Something passes between you.
You eat well for days. That is also nature.

encounters.text: A still puddle shows your reflection. You look bigger than you remember.

effects.log: You know your own shape better now.
The bigger you vanishes. The real one feels lighter.

encounters.text: The wind brings news from far away: smoke, salt, and something old waking up.

ok.log: You find a place where old qi pools.

fail.log: You find only more wind.

effects.log: One day, you will know what it meant.

encounters.text: A patch of sun, warm and perfectly shaped for you. The world can wait.

effects.log: The best sleep of the year.
Rest, mostly, and safety.
Discipline. The patch of sun forgives you.

encounters.text: A root feels its way down toward you and stops. Whatever grows above has found the edge of you.

effects.log: It threads you like a needle through cloth. Above, a bean plant comes up unreasonably green.
The root turns aside, puzzled. A small refusal, kept.
It grows toward the warmth all season. You are, briefly, a gardener.

encounters.text: Feet go over you, many of them, all one way. Through the clay you can tell the ones carrying loads from the ones carrying grudges.

effects.log: Forty-one pairs. Nineteen of them are afraid of something at the far end.

choices.text: Follow one pair as far as the ground goes

effects.log: You lose it at the edge of the damp. It was in a great hurry.
They pass. The ground has not noticed you minded.

encounters.text: The water in the ground has moved. A finger-width in a season, but a well somewhere will notice.

ok.log: The water comes home. Up the slope, a pail comes up full.

fail.log: It will not be led. You settle for the leaving of it.

choices.text: Send it where the well is

effects.log: Somebody above says a prayer to the wrong god, and is not corrected.
It does. Water has always known more than you.

encounters.text: A worm tunnels through your edge and leaves a thread of air behind it. For one afternoon part of you can breathe.

effects.log: It is cold and tastes of roots. You did not know what you were missing.
The worm goes on, none the wiser. You are whole and a little sorry.

choices.text: Follow its tunnel with your attention

effects.log: It goes a surprisingly long way, and meets a root, and a stone, and a bone.

encounters.text: Someone is digging. A spade, then another, careless and shallow. They stop an arm's length from you and sit down to argue.

effects.log: They argue about a boundary stone and go away without finding you.
The spade bites once, rings, and is left standing. Nobody digs there again.
One of them remarks on it. The other says it is the sun. It is not the sun.

encounters.text: Something small has been put into the ground near you: a bowl, a coin, a jar with a name on it. Nobody said what it was for.

effects.log: You hold it as you hold everything, without opinion. It is a small, round weight, and yours.
In a season it is only more clay. The name goes last.

choices.text: Listen to what was said over it

effects.log: A grandmother, to nobody: be good to the new house. You make the clay a degree warmer.

encounters.text: A vein of qi runs under you, thin and slow, the way a thought moves through someone asleep.

effects.log: It tastes of deep stone. You are taller by a hair, which is a long way for clay.

ok.log: It leads to a place with no light and a great calm. You remember it for years.

fail.log: It narrows to a thread and you are back, a little dizzy.

effects.log: It goes on as it has gone on. Some things are not yours to drink.

encounters.text: Frost gets into the ground and lifts everything a hair, then sets it down wrong. You spend the night putting the world back.

effects.log: By dawn the fence post is straight again. Nobody thanks the frost or you.

choices.text: Let it be wrong for one season

effects.log: The gate sticks until spring. You find you do not mind.
The house is level. The yard is a mess. A fair trade.

encounters.text: A child lies with an ear to the ground, listening for what is under it, and gasps when you almost answer.

effects.log: The child runs for the house, delighted and terrified, and will tell the story for sixty years.
The child shrugs and pulls up a clover. Nothing is lost.

choices.text: Warm the patch under the ear

effects.log: The child falls asleep there. You hold very still until supper.

encounters.text: A buried stone near you has been talking for four hundred years and has not repeated itself once.

effects.log: It is about a river that is no longer there. You feel it was a good river.
It does not answer questions. It tells you about the river again, differently.

choices.text: Tell it about your own year

effects.log: The stone says nothing at all, which is the kindest thing it has ever said.

twists.text: Somewhere far off, a temple bell rings once and stops.
A crow follows you for a while, then loses interest.
Your stomach growls loudly, ruining any dignity the moment had.
For a breath the light turns gold, as if the sky is remembering something.
You think of your first teacher, and how they would have laughed at this.
A light rain begins, too fine to be worth complaining about.
The smell of someone's cooking drifts on the wind and breaks your concentration.
An old wound aches, the way it does before the weather turns.
A butterfly lands on your sleeve and stays longer than seems polite.
Somewhere behind you a dog barks, and another answers from far away.
Your sandal strap is about to break. It is a day for small dooms.
The wind changes and brings the smell of snow, though it is not the season.
A broken kite string trails from a branch overhead, swaying in no wind you can feel.
You hum an old song without meaning to, and cannot remember the second verse.
A pair of cranes passes overhead. People say that is lucky. People say many things.
Clouds pile up in the west like the walls of a city in the sky.
A gust takes your hat. You decide it was not a good hat anyway.
Distant thunder rolls, with no cloud in sight.
You remember last night's dream in sudden, useless detail.
A peddler's bell jingles somewhere on the road, never getting closer.
An ant hauls a crumb bigger than itself across your path. You step around it, out of respect.
The moon rises early, pale as a fingernail.
You feel watched, the way you always do in a new place.
The clouds part for a moment and make everything look more important than it is.
Your qi turns once in your dantian, like a fish rolling over in deep water.
A flight of golden phoenixes crosses the sky, and every immortal pretends not to stare.
Far below the clouds, a mortal city lights its lamps.
Somewhere a heavenly clerk sneezes, and a small storm happens in the world below.
Peach blossom drifts down from nowhere, smelling of honey and old victories.
You remember the mortal world: its mud, its rice, its short and urgent lives.
A celestial drum beats once, marking the end of another hundred years.
The light here never moves, but for a moment you could swear it flickered.
A passing immortal nods to you, and you remember when nobody did.
The clouds underfoot ripple, as if something huge swims beneath them.
A thread of silver music hangs in the air and slowly unravels.
Your shadow here is pale gold, and you are still not used to it.
Somewhere a jade gong is struck, and every bird in heaven falls silent.
The stars overhead are close enough to hear them ringing.
A small cloud follows you about like a lost puppy.
The scent of incense rises from far below: someone, somewhere, is praying.
Your nose catches the smell of rain an hour before it comes.
A cricket sings right beside you and will not stop.
The wind ruffles you the wrong way, and you shake it off, irritated.
Far away, a human bell rings, thin and strange.
You remember the warmth of the place you were born, and then it fades.
Your hunger nags at you like a small, rude animal living inside.
The moon follows you across the sky, as it always does.
A tick has found you. This is now the most important thing in the world.
Somewhere below, a dog barks at the mountain, and at you.
The air tastes of iron and pine and coming snow.
Your shadow is longer than it was last year.
A swarm of gnats dances in a sunbeam, very pleased with itself.
Crows gossip in the trees about you, and they are not kind.
The scent of humans hangs faintly over everything, like smoke.
A falling leaf lands on your nose, and you sneeze.
The ground is warm, and you have half a mind to sleep right here.
Thunder grumbles far off, like a big animal clearing its throat.
An owl calls twice, and every small thing in the dark goes quiet.
You dreamed last night of being enormous. It felt like a memory.
The qi in your core turns over slowly, like a stone in a stream.
Somewhere above, a plough turns a furrow and misses you by a hand.
A cart goes over you and the whole ground hums for an hour.
A child hops over the place where you lie, on one foot, for luck.
The clay has a slow, damp itch where a root is growing.
Warmth gathers in you for no reason, then drifts away.
A mole goes by and does not notice you are anything but earth.
The ground settles a little, like a sleeper turning over.
A hundred small weights shift above you and are still.
